cards.info: What must be done to mixed dimensions before calculating volume?
cards.backInfo: All dimensions must be converted to a single common base unit first.

cards.info: What is the conversion factor between meters and centimeters?
cards.backInfo: $1$ meter = $100$ centimeters.

cards.info: How many liters are in one cubic meter ($1\text{ m}^3$)?
cards.backInfo: There are $1000$ liters in $1\text{ m}^3$.

cards.info: How do you convert a measurement from centimeters to meters?
cards.backInfo: Divide the value in centimeters by $100$.

cards.info: What is the definition of dimensional analysis?
cards.backInfo: The algebraic process of multiplying by conversion factors so unwanted units cancel.

cards.info: Why is multiplying centimeters by meters directly a mistake for volume?
cards.backInfo: It prevents a direct conversion to liters and creates inconsistent units.

cards.info: When converting $\text{m}^3$ to liters, how should the numerical value change?
cards.backInfo: The numerical value should increase by a factor of $1000$.

cards.info: What is the liquid capacity of a $1.0\text{ m} \times 1.0\text{ m} \times 1.0\text{ m}$ container?
cards.backInfo: The capacity is exactly $1000$ liters.

cards.info: Why convert linear units to meters before calculating volume for liters?
cards.backInfo: It is more direct than calculating cubic centimeters first.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the steps: Convert all to meters, Multiply for m^3, Multiply by 1000 for Liters.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/96a4c4f6-1789-498c-af09-89996f4f4865-1786505531254-913.webp)

cards.info: What is the final step in the Unit-Chain strategy for volume?
cards.backInfo: Apply the conversion factor from cubic meters ($\text{m}^3$) to liters (L).

cards.info: Why is it harder to convert units after they have been cubed?
cards.backInfo: Converting linear units to meters first is more direct than converting cubic units.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the steps: Convert all to meters, Multiply for m^3, Multiply by 1000 for Liters.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/96a4c4f6-1789-498c-af09-89996f4f4865-1786505531254-913.webp)

cards.info: If a dimension is $120\text{ cm}$, what is its length in meters?
cards.backInfo: The length is $1.20\text{ meters}$ because $1\text{ m} = 100\text{ cm}$.

cards.info: What conversion factor changes $0.18\text{ m}^3$ into $180\text{ L}$?
cards.backInfo: Multiply by the factor $1000\text{ L} / 1\text{ m}^3$.

cards.info: To convert $150\text{ cm}$ to meters, what arithmetic operation is performed?
cards.backInfo: Divide $150$ by $100$ to get $1.50\text{ m}$.

cards.info: In dimensional analysis, where should the unit you want to remove be?
cards.backInfo: The unit to be removed should be in the denominator of the fraction.

cards.info: How is a volume result in $\text{m}^3$ achieved from linear measurements?
cards.backInfo: By multiplying three distinct linear measurements that are all expressed in meters.

cards.info: What is the error in calculating volume as $150\text{ cm} \times 0.40\text{ m} \times 0.30\text{ m}$?
cards.backInfo: Multiplying dimensions in different units without converting to a common unit first.

cards.info: If your volume calculation changes from $0.15$ to $150$, what conversion occurred?
cards.backInfo: A conversion from cubic meters to liters ($0.15 \times 1000 = 150$).

cards.info: A tank measures $1\text{ m}$ on all sides. How many liters does it hold?
cards.backInfo: It holds $1000$ liters because $1\text{ m} \times 1\text{ m} \times 1\text{ m} = 1\text{ m}^3$.

cards.info: In $0.15\text{ m}^3 \times (1000\text{ L} / 1\text{ m}^3)$, why is $1\text{ m}^3$ in the denominator?
cards.backInfo: It is required to cancel the $\text{m}^3$ unit in the numerator.
